extracted.intended_audience: students, researchers, and practitioners in journalism, media/communication studies, and photojournalism
extracted.subtask_description: Frameworks and conceptual dimensions for analysing photographs in newspapers and online news, focusing on how meanings are made, text–image relations, composition, news values, and changing practices in photojournalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introducing the multisemiotic news story
rubrics_metrics.description: An orientation to treating news stories as multisemiotic: composed of multiple semiotic resources (images, text, layout) that together produce meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book 'introducing the multisemiotic news story' frames news items as multimodal ensembles; analysis should consider how different semiotic modes interact rather than treating images or text in isolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: News values and the multisemiotic news story
rubrics_metrics.description: News values as they operate across multiple semiotic modes within the news story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how conventional news values (e.g., timeliness, proximity, prominence, conflict) are signalled or reinforced by images and by the interplay of image and text. The chapter 'News values and the multisemiotic news story' implies assessing value not only in headlines but in visual choices and placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: The multiple functionality of news images
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition that a single news photograph can perform several functions (informational, evidential, emotive, rhetorical, symbolic) within a news story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses should identify and differentiate the functions an image is performing in context (e.g., illustrating facts, providing eyewitness evidence, eliciting empathy, offering commentary). The book emphasises that images have multiple, simultaneous roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition and aesthetic value in press photography
rubrics_metrics.description: Composition and aesthetic qualities of press photographs contribute to their meaning and value within news discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors should examine formal elements (composition, framing, lighting, perspective) and how aesthetic decisions affect interpretation, credibility, and newsworthiness, as indicated by the chapter 'Composition and aesthetic value in press photography.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Text–image relations: Image as nucleus
rubrics_metrics.description: Situations where the image acts as the nucleus (central, organizing element) of the news discourse, with text functioning to support or expand the image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify cases where the photograph carries the core proposition or narrative and evaluate how accompanying text supplements, explains, or negotiates that visual core (from 'Text-image relations in news discourse Part 1: Image as Nucleus').

rubrics_metrics.name: Text–image relations: Image as satellite
rubrics_metrics.description: Situations where the image plays a satellite role (supportive, subordinate) to a primarily text-centred news story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine how images add illustrative detail, human interest, or emotive color without being the primary carrier of the story, and judge coherence between image and text (from 'Text-image relations in news discourse Part 2: Image as Satellite').

rubrics_metrics.name: Text–image relations: Sequences of images
rubrics_metrics.description: The narrative and interpretive effects produced by sequences or series of images within news coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyse how ordering, selection, and juxtaposition of multiple images create temporal, causal, or thematic narratives; consider sequencing as a multimodal resource (from 'Text-image relations in news discourse Part 3: Sequences of images').

rubrics_metrics.name: Evolving practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Awareness of continuity and change in practices, styles, norms and values of photojournalism, especially in the digital age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate photographic practices and editorial choices in light of technological, institutional, and cultural changes in online and print news environments (chapter 'Evolving practices' and related referenced chapters such as 'News Photography and the Digital (R)evolution').

rubrics_metrics.name: Tools for systematic interpretation of press photographs
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of analytic tools and methods to systematically analyse press photographs and their relations to text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book offers 'a set of useful tools for their interpretation'—practitioners should apply structured, multimodal analysis techniques (e.g., semiotic/resource-based categories, function identification, composition analysis) and use authentic news stories as exemplars.
